h1: Sunee View Hotel — a small, quiet city hotel in Chachoengsao within walking distance of Wat Sothon
intro: If you're heading to Chachoengsao to pay your respects to Luang Pho Sothon and want a place that's close enough to walk to the temple, quiet, with free parking, and only a few hundred baht a night — Sunee View Hotel hits the mark for pilgrims and budget travellers alike · It's a small in-town hotel on Soi 7, Thep Khunakon Road, Sothon Subdistrict, Mueang Chachoengsao District, only about 1 kilometre from Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan · Rooms are clean with a fridge, TV, and AC, some have a balcony, and there's a garden to sit in, an on-site restaurant, bikes to borrow, and a little spot to fish · Rooms start at about THB 550/night, with a real-guest score of around 8.2; what people consistently mention is the location near the temple, the quiet, and the attentive staff

body.html: Who Sunee View Hotel is right for — to put it as simply as possible, Sunee View Hotel is a small city hotel for people who come to Chachoengsao to visit Wat Sothon, handle errands, or stop over for the night and want a room that's clean, quiet, and easy on the wallet · This isn't a riverside resort with a pool and spa, and it isn't a luxury hotel with every service on tap · It's a compact place in Sothon Subdistrict, in one of the closest spots to Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan where you can actually find a room · Its selling points are clear: a location you can walk to the temple from, a quiet atmosphere, and prices that start at just over five hundred baht · Real guest reviews line up on this — the people it suits best are older travellers and merit-making families coming to the temple, workers in town on business, and road-trippers looking for a budget place with parking, rather than anyone hunting for a resort-style stay to photograph or a full-day staycation · Another group that says they were impressed is people who want genuine quiet, because the hotel sits on a soi that isn't busy, with no big trucks rumbling past all night, which suits anyone who wants a solid night's sleep before an early start at the temple · It plays the "close to the temple and good value" card to the hilt, trading off the fact that it has fewer amenities than a larger hotel

Location and getting around — this is Sunee View Hotel's number-one strength, no question · The hotel sits on Soi 7, Thep Khunakon Road, Sothon Subdistrict, Mueang Chachoengsao District, only about 1 kilometre from Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan, which is very close compared with many places in the province that mean driving several kilometres · A distance like that means plenty of people can comfortably walk to Luang Pho Sothon in the morning before the crowds, or drive there in just a few minutes · Nearby, Wat Bang Phra is about 600 metres away, and the Luang Pho Sothon shrine and the temple grounds are within easy reach all day · A little farther out, Paet Riu Railway Station (Chachoengsao Station) is about 5–6 kilometres away, handy for anyone arriving by train and continuing into town · The town of Chachoengsao, the markets, and various restaurants are all a short drive of under ten minutes · One thing to know if you're flying in: the hotel is about 45 kilometres from Suvarnabhumi Airport, roughly a 45-minute to one-hour drive depending on traffic · Because it's a small hotel down a soi, anyone driving themselves has the advantage of free private parking and won't have to worry about where to leave the car · One small note: the hotel is down a soi, so finding the way in the first time may take a careful look at the map, and the shops around it aren't as dense as the town centre, so if you want plenty of food options you may need to drive out a little

"We chose this place because it's so close to Wat Sothon — you can walk over to pay your respects in the morning. The hotel is quiet, we slept well, and the staff were kind and helpful. At this price it's great value for a merit-making trip."

Room types and decor — Sunee View Hotel is a small hotel, and the main room on offer is the Deluxe Studio with a king bed, an air-conditioned studio with a window that lets in natural light · Inside you get a flat-screen TV, fridge, air conditioning, and a private bathroom with a shower and toiletries · A detail many people like is that some rooms have a balcony to step out onto for fresh air and a view of the garden, which feels more open than a fully enclosed room · The decor is simple and clean — not luxurious, but built for real use, well suited to a one- or two-night stay · Real reviews single out the cleanliness of the rooms as a point of praise, and some mention the bathroom plumbing, with hot water that works well and good water pressure — the kind of detail small-hotel guests care about · One thing to keep in mind: some reviews say the mattress is on the firm side for some people, even though the hotel does provide a topper, so anyone who likes a soft bed may want to ask at check-in · Overall, the rooms at Sunee View do their job as clean, wallet-friendly bedrooms, best approached with the expectations of a budget city hotel rather than the luxury of a suite

Amenities, garden, and activities — small as it is, Sunee View Hotel has a few touches that set the mood apart from a typical city hotel · One thing people mention is the garden and shady outdoor space where guests can sit and relax, which makes it feel like a private, quiet stay rather than just a shophouse on the roadside · The hotel also offers bike rental for anyone who wants to ride around or pedal to the temple, and has a fishing spot — a small touch you don't often find at this price · On the basics for a budget stay, it has what you need — free private parking, free Wi-Fi, and a 24-hour reception, with staff who speak both Thai and English · There's an on-site restaurant so you can order food without going far · To be straight about it, there's no swimming pool, no fitness room, and no spa, because this is a small hotel that leans on quiet and a low price rather than resort-style amenities · So if you're planning a staycation that needs a pool for the kids or pretty photo corners, this may not be the right fit, and you should consider a Bangpakong riverside stay or a resort in the same set instead

Food and breakfast — set your expectations right on food at Sunee View Hotel · The hotel has an on-site restaurant where you can order food, which is handy for anyone who doesn't want to drive far in the evening to find something to eat · Some reviews speak positively of the à la carte breakfast, but there's no big buffet breakfast like at a larger hotel · For anyone wanting more variety, the in-town location helps, because a short drive into Chachoengsao town turns up restaurants, cafés, and the town markets, including the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market, a well-known food spot · Many people coming for the temple tend to look for food around Wat Sothon, which already has plenty of restaurants and souvenir stalls, since it's only about a kilometre from the hotel · On the whole, food at Sunee View isn't a reason to come and eat at the hotel itself; it's a useful add-on that makes things more convenient, in keeping with using the hotel as a base to head out for merit-making and to explore the town

Service — service is another point that earns steady praise in real reviews · Most voices agree that the staff are friendly, kind, and helpful, whether with check-in, directions to the temple, or general care during the stay · Being a small hotel makes contact with the staff close and quick, without the layers of process you get at a big hotel · The reception is open 24 hours, so anyone arriving late or leaving before dawn can rest easy that someone is on hand · Staff communicate in both Thai and English, so they look after Thai guests and visiting foreign travellers alike · This is the charm of a small, attentively run place, and many people say it feels more like staying at a relative's house than at a hotel

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com, and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a walkable location near Wat Sothon, a quiet atmosphere that makes for easy sleep, clean rooms, friendly and helpful staff, free parking that's handy for self-drivers, hot water in the bathroom that works well with good pressure, and prices that are great value for what you get · On the watch-out side: what comes up is a mattress that's on the firm side for some people (though a topper is provided), it being a small hotel with no resort-style amenities like a pool or fitness room, the hotel being down a soi that may be a bit hard to find the first time, and the shops around being sparse, so you'll need to drive into town if you want plenty of food options · These criticisms are manageable by setting expectations correctly — a budget city hotel that leans on a location near the temple and on quiet — rather than being big problems that put people off coming back · A real-guest score of around 8.2 and the word "value" coming up often reflect that most people are happy with what they paid for
"Clean, quiet room, hot water with good pressure, and a very low price. The only gripe is the mattress is a touch firm, but you can ask for a topper. On the whole it's worth what you pay."

Price comparison and value — Sunee View Hotel's starting price is about THB 550/night for a Deluxe Studio in the normal range, and it can edge up over long weekends or during Wat Sothon festival periods · Compared with other places in Chachoengsao town that start at around THB 700–900 and up, Sunee View is in one of the cheapest groups, while still giving you a clean room, free parking, and a location closer to Wat Sothon than many others · The value here isn't in luxury amenities, but in paying little and getting the best location for visiting the temple, plus quiet and parking — the three things pilgrims and budget travellers care about most · If you're planning a Chachoengsao trip for merit-making or a quick errand and don't need a pool or a resort feel, every baht spent on this place pays off fully in location and quiet · But if you can stretch the budget a little more for a riverside resort or a pool, there are other options in the province better suited to that

Good to know before you book — a few things help the stay go smoothly · One, if your main aim is to visit Wat Sothon, make the most of that roughly 1-kilometre distance and plan an early start, walking or a short drive over to pay your respects before the crowds · Two, if you like a soft bed, ask about a topper at check-in, since reviews say the mattress is on the firm side for some people · Three, if you want a room with a balcony, specify it at the time of booking or ask first, because not every room has one · Four, if you're driving yourself, pull up a map and pin the location of Soi 7, Thep Khunakon Road carefully, because the hotel is down a soi you may not spot right away the first time, but free parking is waiting · Five, during the Luang Pho Sothon homage festival (the Wat Sothon fair), hotels in town fill up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and choose a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm · Six, since it's a small hotel, rooms may be limited, so if you're coming as a group, book with time to spare

Summary — from all the real reviews, Sunee View Hotel is the best fit for people coming to Chachoengsao to visit Wat Sothon, run errands, or stop over for the night who want a clean, quiet room, free parking, and a low price · A location only about 1 kilometre from Wat Sothon and walkable, a quiet atmosphere, a garden to sit in, and attentive staff make it great value among the province's affordable places to stay · If you're after a place with a pool, a fitness room, or a resort feel for a full-day getaway, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a Bangpakong riverside resort or a wellness stay in the province instead · But for a merit-making trip or an errand trip where you want the closest location to the temple, along with quiet and a friendly price — Sunee View Hotel is an option that does its job well and fits its crowd

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Sunee View Hotel Chachoengsao

faq.q: Where is Sunee View Hotel in Chachoengsao, and is it close to Wat Sothon?
faq.a: Sunee View Hotel is at 58/59 Soi 7, Thep Khunakon Road, Sothon Subdistrict, Mueang Chachoengsao District · It's only about 1 kilometre from Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan (Luang Pho Sothon) and walkable · Wat Bang Phra is about 600 metres away, and the town of Chachoengsao is a short drive in.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Sunee View Hotel, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 550/night for a Deluxe Studio with a king bed · It's an air-conditioned studio with a window, flat-screen TV, fridge, and a private bathroom · Some rooms have a balcony, so specify it when booking · Prices vary by season, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Sunee View Hotel have free parking and Wi-Fi?
faq.a: It has both · Free private parking, handy for self-drivers, and free Wi-Fi · There's a 24-hour reception with Thai- and English-speaking staff, plus bike rental and a fishing spot on site.

faq.q: Does Sunee View Hotel have breakfast and a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's no buffet breakfast and no swimming pool · But there's an on-site restaurant where you can order food, and some reviews speak positively of the à la carte breakfast · The area around Wat Sothon nearby also has plenty of restaurants and food · This place is about a clean, low-priced room near the temple, not a resort with full amenities.

faq.q: Who is Sunee View Hotel right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people coming to visit Wat Sothon, make merit, run errands, or stop over for the night who want a clean, quiet room with free parking at a low price · It suits older travellers, merit-making families, and self-drivers · If you want a pool or a riverside resort feel, you may want to look at other places in this set instead.

faq.q: What are the review scores for Sunee View Hotel like?
faq.a: The real-guest score is around 8.2 on Trip.com and about 8.1 on Booking.com · The most praised points are the location near Wat Sothon, the quiet, clean rooms, attentive staff, and value for money · Points to keep in mind are a mattress that's on the firm side for some people (a topper is provided) and the lack of resort-style amenities.
